turns.prompt_text: What are the dimensions of a langstros hive deep super? Can you show me a diagram like a engineering diagram
turns.response_html:
In the beekeeping world, the Deep Super (often called the "Deep Hive Body") is the standard large box used for the brood chamber. While there are 8-frame and 10-frame variations, the heights and lengths remain consistent across the industry to ensure frames are interchangeable.

Standard Dimensions (10-Frame Deep)

Most commercial beekeeping equipment is built using 3/4" (19mm) thick lumber.

DimensionExternalInternal
Length19 7/8"18 3/8"
Width16 1/4"14 3/4"
Height (Depth)9 5/8"9 5/8"

Note: For an 8-frame hive, the external width is reduced to 14" (internal width of 12 1/2"), but all other dimensions remain the same.

Engineering Schematic (Cross-Section)

The critical mechanical feature of a hive box is the rabbet cut (frame rest) at the top of the end boards. This allows the frames to hang while maintaining "bee space" (the specific gap bees won't fill with wax or propolis).

Critical Tolerances

  • The Frame Rest: A notch is cut into the top inside edge of the two shorter (front/back) boards. The standard cut is 5/8" deep and 3/8" wide.
  • Bee Space: The internal height of the box (9 5/8") compared to the standard deep frame height (9 1/8") leaves a 1/2" gap. This allows for 1/4" of space above and below the frames when boxes are stacked, which is the "Goldilocks" zone for bee movement.
  • Material: If you are machining your own, ensure you use weather-resistant wood like Cedar or Cypress, or high-grade Pine that is well-painted on the exterior.

Would you like the specific dimensions for the frames that fit inside this box as well?
